data.title: Gold settles below $4,000 after steepest weekly loss in nearly five months
data.description:
Gold futures fell to three-month lows and silver slumped to its lowest level in nearly a year on ‌Friday, as higher energy prices added to inflation concerns and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain restrictive monetary policy.

Brent crude oil closed at its highest level in six months as as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia continued to raise concerns over further disruption to energy supplies and traders bet on renewed fighting in the Middle East after the U.S. midterm election on November 3.

The selloff in tech stocks has also led to margin calls for ​equity traders and investors, causing them to sell gold and silver assets, American Gold Exchange analyst Jim Wyckoff said in a note.

"A rising inflation backdrop along with selling pressure to cover losses in equity or bond market positions is a negative combination for gold in the short-term, even as the Fed is looking assured to keep rates unchanged at next week's FOMC meeting," MUFG's Soojin Kim wrote.

Traders broadly expect the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming October 27-28 meeting, but they see a 78% probability of a hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Two main factors are behind gold's recent swoon, Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital said in a note - "First, investors are raising cash; second, Russia is selling gold holdings as the war continues to leave its economy in shambles" - but "while the risk of further downside remains, we would selectively buy at these levels."

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for October delivery fell 1.3% on Friday to $3,991.10/oz, its lowest settlement value since July 16, and front-month Comex October silver (XAGUSD:CUR) slumped 1.9% to $53.711/oz, its lowest close since November 26, 2025.

For the week, gold and silver fell 4% and 5.7%, respectively.

data.description:

SpaceX-related competitive pressure contributed to the slide. Peer TMUS fell 8% as well.T has fallen about 16% in the past month

data.title: Bristol, Tempus AI partnering with Pathos AI to advance neurological treatments
data.description:
• Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) will collaborate with Pathos AI to utilize the latter's agentic AI platform, Foundry, to build a specialized, curated dataset and agentic AI capabilities for Alzheimer’s disease and other neurological ailments.
  • Also, Bristol is the lead in the AI firm's Series E financing.
  • Though the three-year deal, "BMS aims to generate deeper insights into disease progression, identify patients most likely to benefit from potential therapies and design more precise clinical trials," per a news release.
  • Tempus AI (TEM) inked a separate deal with Pathos AI to apply the former's expertise in oncology "to create a comprehensive, de-identified, longitudinal dataset from hundreds of thousands of patients with neurological conditions, designed to track outcomes over time and accelerate biological insight." 
  • Terms call for Pathos to license the data from Tempus in a five-year, $55M agreement.

data.title: Comfort Systems USA drops 9% after earnings, CFO retirement

FIX closed at $1,160.86, a decline of $118.51, as volume reached approximately 1.37 million shares, roughly 3.6 times the one-month average. This added to a recent retreat, including a nearly 9% drop on Thursday.

data.title: Corcept Therapeutics plunges 20% on Genmab cancer data
data.description:
Shares of Corcept Therapeutics (CORT), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on cortisol modulation, sank 20% on Friday. The stock dropped $21.64 to end at $85.86 with volume of roughly 2.86 million shares, a relative volume of 3.78 times the one-month average.

The slide came after Genmab reported that a phase 3 trial of its antibody-drug conjugate, rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S), met its primary goal for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. CORT, which markets Lifyorli (relacorilant) for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, dropped on the news.

data.title: IC Group restructures leadership, targets $900K in annual savings
data.description:
• IC Group (ICGH:CA) announced a leadership restructuring on Friday, with COO Marc Caron departing and other non-officer positions eliminated, effective immediately.
  • The company expects a Q4 FY2026 restructuring charge of approximately $1M, mainly for severance and employee transition costs.
  • The changes are expected to generate annual savings of approximately $900K.
  • CEO Duncan McCready said the changes aim to simplify decision-making, improve accountability, and focus resources on key growth priorities.
  • The restructuring charge is expected to be paid over the next 14 months.
